content: During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if it is clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can reduce the levels of atovaquone in your body, potentially affecting its efficacy. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not freeze this product, as freezing can reduce the amount of atovaquone your body absorbs, potentially decreasing its effectiveness. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Atovaquone is used to prevent or treat a serious lung infection called Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP). How to Use: Shake the bottle gently but thoroughly before each dose. Measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. To treat PCP, take this medication by mouth with food as directed by your doctor, usually twice daily for 21 days. To prevent PCP, take this medication with food, usually once daily as directed. This medication works best when the amount of medicine in your body is kept at a constant level. If you take this drug twice daily, take it at evenly spaced intervals, approximately 12 hours apart. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, trouble sleeping, or a runny nose. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Atovaquone can commonly cause a mild rash that is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking atovaquone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate dizziness. Do not drive, use machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk.
